sanskrit: prataś ca yasya saprataś ca nāmānuṣṭubhasya haviṣo havir yat | dhātur dyutānāt savituś ca viṣṇo rathaṃtaram ā jabhārā vasiṣṭhaḥ ||
english: Whose name is Pratha and Sapratha — the oblation of the Anuṣṭubh, the offering of that offering — from Dhātṛ the resplendent, from Savitṛ and from Viṣṇu, Vasiṣṭha brought forth the Rathaṃtara Sāman.

sanskrit: avindan te atihitaṃ yad āsīd yajñasya dhāma paramaṃ guhā yat | dhātur dyutānāt savituś ca viṣṇor bharadvājo bṛhad ā cakre agneḥ ||
english: They found what had been hidden away — the supreme seat of sacrifice that lay in secret: from Dhātṛ the resplendent, from Savitṛ and Viṣṇu, from Agni, Bharadvāja fashioned the Bṛhat Sāman.

sanskrit: te 'vindan manasā dīdhyānā yajuḥ ṣkannam prathamaṃ devayānam | dhātur dyutānāt savituś ca viṣṇor ā sūryād abharan gharmam ete ||
english: Meditating with the mind, they found the spilled Yajus verse — the first, the path of the gods — from Dhātṛ the resplendent, from Savitṛ and Viṣṇu; these ones brought the gharma (the hot-milk oblation) down from the Sun.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatir nayatu durgahā tiraḥ punar neṣad aghaśaṃsāya manma | kṣipad aśastim apa durmatim hann athā karad yajamānāya śaṃ yoḥ ||
english: May Bṛhaspati lead us through the difficult passes; may he not guide thought toward the evil-tongued again. Driving away the curse, smiting malevolence, may he then make wellbeing and peace for the sacrificer.

sanskrit: narāśaṃso no 'vatu prayāje śaṃ no astv anuyājo haveṣu | kṣipad aśastim apa durmatim hann athā karad yajamānāya śaṃ yoḥ ||
english: May Narāśaṃsa protect us at the fore-oblation; may there be well-being for us at the after-oblation, in our invocations. Driving away the curse, smiting malevolence, may he then make wellbeing and peace for the sacrificer.

sanskrit: tapurmūrdhā tapatu rakṣaso ye brahmadviṣaḥ śarave hantavā u | kṣipad aśastim apa durmatim hann athā karad yajamānāya śaṃ yoḥ ||
english: He of the burning head — let him scorch those rākṣasas who hate the sacred word and deserve the arrow of slaying. Driving away the curse, smiting malevolence, may he then make wellbeing and peace for the sacrificer.

sanskrit: apaśyaṃ tvā manasā cekitānaṃ tapaso jātaṃ tapaso vibhūtam | iha prajām iha rayiṃ rarāṇaḥ pra jāyasva prajayā putrakāma ||
english: I saw you with the mind, wide-awake, born of tapas, manifested through tapas; bestowing offspring here, bestowing wealth here — come forth with progeny, O you who desires a son.

sanskrit: apaśyaṃ tvā manasā dīdhyānāṃ svāyāṃ tanū ṛtvye nādhamānām | upa mām uccā yuvatir babhūyāḥ pra jāyasva prajayā putrakāme ||
english: I saw you with the mind, meditating, yearning in your own body in the season's time; may the young woman come up to me — come forth with progeny, O you who desires a son.

sanskrit: ahaṃ garbham adadhām oṣadhīṣv ahaṃ viśveṣu bhuvaneṣv antaḥ | aham prajā ajanayam pṛthivyām ahaṃ janibhyo aparīṣu putrān ||
english: I placed the embryo in the plants; I dwell within all the worlds. I have engendered offspring upon the earth; I have given sons to mothers thereafter born.

sanskrit: viṣṇur yoniṃ kalpayatu tvaṣṭā rūpāṇi piṃśatu | ā siñcatu prajāpatir dhātā garbhaṃ dadhātu te ||
english: Let Viṣṇu prepare the womb; let Tvaṣṭṛ fashion the forms; let Prajāpati pour the seed; and let Dhātṛ, the ordainer, establish the embryo in you.

sanskrit: garbhaṃ dhehi sinīvāli garbhaṃ dhehi sarasvati | garbhaṃ te aśvinau devāv ā dhattām puṣkarasrajā ||
english: Place the embryo, O Sinīvālī; place the embryo, O Sarasvatī; may the two divine Aśvins, garlanded with lotuses, place the embryo in you.

sanskrit: hiraṇyayī araṇī yaṃ nirmanthato aśvinā | taṃ te garbhaṃ havāmahe daśame māsi sūtave ||
english: The golden fire-drill which the two Aśvins churn together — that embryo we invoke for you, to be brought to birth in the tenth month.

sanskrit: mahi trīṇām avo 'stu dyukṣam mitrasyāryamṇaḥ | durādharṣaṃ varuṇasya ||
english: Great and heaven-abiding be the aid of the three — of Mitra and of Aryaman — and irresistible the protection of Varuṇa.

sanskrit: nahi teṣām amā cana nādhvasu vāraṇeṣu | īśe ripur aghaśaṃsaḥ ||
english: Neither at home, nor on the roads, nor in the mountain strongholds does the evil-minded foe, the evil-tongued, hold sway against them.

sanskrit: yasmai putrāso aditeḥ pra jīvase martyāya | jyotir yacchanti ajasram ||
english: For that mortal to whom the sons of Aditi extend the unceasing light, that he may live.

sanskrit: vāta ā vātu bheṣajaṃ śambhu mayobhu no hṛde | pra ṇa āyūṃṣi tāriṣat ||
english: Let the Wind blow its medicine — bringing ease, bringing bliss — to our heart; may he prolong our spans of life.

sanskrit: uta vāta pitāsi na uta bhrātota naḥ sakhā | sa no jīvātave kṛdhi ||
english: And you, O Wind, are our father, and our brother, and our friend — make us live.

sanskrit: yad ado vāta te gṛhe 'mṛtasya nidhir hitaḥ | tato no dehi jīvase ||
english: That which yonder, O Wind, in your house has been laid up as a store of immortality — from that, grant us life.

sanskrit: prāgnaye vācam īraya vṛṣabhāya kṣitīnām | sa naḥ parṣad ati dviṣaḥ ||
english: Send forth your voice to Agni, the bull of the peoples; may he carry us across and beyond the hostile.

sanskrit: yaḥ parasyāḥ parāvatas tiro dhanvātirocat | sa naḥ parṣad ati dviṣaḥ ||
english: He who shines forth across the far distance, across the desert wasteland — may he carry us across and beyond the hostile.

sanskrit: yo rakṣāṃsi nijūrvati vṛṣā śukreṇa śociṣā | sa naḥ parṣad ati dviṣaḥ ||
english: He who, the bull, drives back the rākṣasas with his bright and pure flame — may he carry us across and beyond the hostile.

sanskrit: yo viśvābhi vipaśyati bhuvanā saṃ ca paśyati | sa naḥ parṣad ati dviṣaḥ ||
english: He who gazes out over all the worlds and beholds them together as one — may he carry us across and beyond the hostile.

sanskrit: yo asya pāre rajasaḥ śukro agnir ajāyata | sa naḥ parṣad ati dviṣaḥ ||
english: The bright Agni who was born on the far shore of this realm of space — may he carry us across and beyond the hostile.

sanskrit: pra nūnaṃ jātavedasam aśvaṃ hinota vājinam | idaṃ no barhir āsade ||
english: Urge forward now Jātavedas, the steed, the swift one — to take his seat upon this our sacred kuśa grass.

sanskrit: asya pra jātavedaso vipravīrasya mīḻhuṣaḥ | mahīm iyarmi suṣṭutim ||
english: Of this Jātavedas, the inspired hero, the bountiful bestower, I send forth the great and excellent praise.

sanskrit: yā ruco jātavedaso devatrā havyavāhanīḥ | tābhir no yajñam invatu ||
english: With those bright flames of Jātavedas that carry the oblation to the gods — with those may he impel our sacrifice.

sanskrit: āyaṃ gauḥ pṛśnir akramīd asadan mātaram puraḥ | pitaraṃ ca prayan svaḥ ||
english: This dappled cow has stepped forward; she has settled before her mother and proceeds toward the father — toward the heavenly light.

sanskrit: antaś carati rocanāsya prāṇād apānatī | vy akhyan mahiṣo divam ||
english: Within the luminous vault she moves, breathing in and out from his breath; the great bull has illumined the sky.

sanskrit: triṃśad dhāma vi rājati vāk pataṃgāya dhīyate | prativastor aha dyubhiḥ ||
english: Thirty stations shine resplendent; speech is directed toward the winged one (the Sun); at each of the two twilights, day by day, through the luminous days.

sanskrit: ṛtaṃ ca satyaṃ cābhīddhāt tapaso 'dhy ajāyata | tato rātry ajāyata tataḥ samudro arṇavaḥ ||
english: From blazing tapas, cosmic order (ṛta) and truth (satya) were born; from that, night was born; from that, the billowing ocean arose.

sanskrit: samudrād arṇavād adhi saṃvatsaro ajāyata | ahorātrāṇi vidad had viśvasya miṣato vaśī ||
english: From the billowing ocean the year was born; he who is master of all that blinks and breathes ordained the days and nights.

sanskrit: sūryācandramasau dhātā yathāpūrvam akalpayat | divaṃ ca pṛthivīṃ cāntarikṣam atho svaḥ ||
english: Dhātṛ, the ordainer, established the Sun and Moon as they were before — heaven and earth, the mid-space, and the realm of celestial light.

sanskrit: saṃ-sam id yuvase vṛṣann agne viśvāny arya ā | iḻas pade sam idhyase sa no vasūny ā bhara ||
english: Together, altogether you kindle all things, O bull, O Agni, O Lord; on the seat of Iḷā you are kindled together — bring to us all good things.

sanskrit: saṃ gacchadhvaṃ saṃ vadadhvaṃ saṃ vo manāṃsi jānatām | devā bhāgaṃ yathā pūrve saṃjānānā upāsate ||
english: Come together, speak together; let your minds be in agreement. As the gods of old, in concord, partook of their appointed share — so may you.

sanskrit: samāno mantraḥ samitiḥ samānī samānam manaḥ saha cittam eṣām | samānam mantram abhi mantraye vaḥ samānena vo haviṣā juhomi ||
english: Common is the counsel, common the assembly, common the mind, and joined together the intention of these; with a common counsel I address you all; with a common oblation I make the offering to you.

sanskrit: samānī va ākūtiḥ samānā hṛdayāni vaḥ | samānam astu vo mano yathā vaḥ susahāsati ||
english: Common be your purpose; common your hearts; let your mind be as one — so that all may go well for you together.
